claim_text: Paired 4-bit QLoRA allocator peaks were 0.54-0.73x the BF16 LoRA peaks across seven observed seed pairs.

8B 4-bit was the largest tested configuration with a completed three-seed preregistered set within one favorable observed machine-state window; runs took 1643-1693 s and allocator peak averaged 9.19 GiB.

Within the two fully paired three-seed scales, observed 4-bit/BF16 step-time ratios were 1.10-1.23 and fell inside the preregistered +/-25% margin; the 4B single cross-window pair is descriptive only.
Across the measured 4-bit scale range, allocator peak memory had log-log slope 0.57 +/- 0.05 (R2=0.99, four group means), which is sublinear over the measured range.
The 4-bit step-time log-log slope was 1.00 +/- 0.09 (R2=0.98); corrected paging strata are mixed, so absolute timing remains window- and tier-scoped.
analysis_status: confirmatory scaling analysis with corrected stratification

claim_text: For 4B 4-bit, the 1024-cap group averaged 24.0 s/step and 11.16 GiB peak; the 2048-cap group averaged 20.7 s/step and 23.88 GiB peak.
Observed maximum-context bracket: the 2048-cap workload completed; the first observed failure was a single-seed synthetic 4096-cap probe. This is not a statistical or physical trainability threshold.
In the valid batch-axis set, throughput decreased from 89.5 to 66.4 to 34.6 token/s for b1/b2/b4 while allocator peak rose from 6.19 to 10.04 to 16.98 GiB.
evidence_grade: three valid seeds per completed batch

claim_text: All three valid 2026-09-15 batch-8 runs terminated before the first completed optimizer step; swap peaks spanned 19.5-20.4 GiB. D5-invalid 2026-09-12 rows do not support this claim.
evidence_grade: three valid runs; one has withheld kernel corroboration

claim_text: For 4B 4-bit, ranks 4/8/32 changed mean step time by less than 2% around the shared rank-8 baseline, while the measured peak range was 0.24 GiB.

The 14B 4-bit boundary evidence includes a completed 20-step probe, a roughly 24-minute zero-step formal observation, and a timeout after 70/100 steps with observed step times 9.4-105.1 s and swap 3.4-9.5 GiB.
For the same 4B BF16 configuration, the high-residency observation made 0 completed-step progress in about 27 minutes, while the zero-residency rerun completed in 451 s with median step time 3.03 s.
evidence_grade: same configuration across two state windows

claim_text: At the frozen learning rate, 0.6B full fine-tuning ended at mean validation loss 4.44, versus 1.93 for 4-bit QLoRA; the full-fine-tuning outcome is retained as a negative result.
The corpus contains 118 finalized runs and 27 failures; 9 D5 implementation-invalid attempts are excluded by signature, 46 runs enter aggregation, and raw-to-processed reconciliation is complete.
After the 100-step benchmark, observed 4-bit minus BF16 final validation-loss differences were 0.1135 at 0.6B and 0.0845 at 1.7B; no converged-quality equivalence is claimed.
Among completed runs, group-mean within-run drift stayed near 1 while step-time dispersion rose in heavier paging regimes; this describes burstiness without establishing a causal mechanism.
The 8B median step time was 10.039 s and its empirical p99 was about 3.1 times the median; the tail metric is descriptive and window-specific.
The 14B timeout completed 70/100 steps and showed an oscillating 3.4-9.5 GiB swap trace; step-level wall-clock alignment is unavailable for the timeout.
The valid batch-8 trio rose by 16.3-17.1 GiB before termination, reaching peaks of 19.5-20.4 GiB with zero completed steps.

Concurrent system swap level had median within-run Spearman rho about +0.22 in Tier-A and +0.10 in Tier-B aligned runs; this is descriptive co-variation under second-resolution and attribution limits.

Memory accounting leaves an unallocated residual for adapter runs; the reported affine slope decomposition is an arithmetic partition of stored-weight and residual slopes, not causal proof of an overhead mechanism.
evidence_grade: measured allocator peaks plus model manifest
